title: Russian Missile and Drone Barrage Across Ukraine Injures at Least 19
excerpt: Overnight strikes on Kyiv, Zaporizhzhia and Odesa land days after Trump's claim of an energy-truce deal — while Ukraine hits a Russian refinery and airbase in return.
body:
• At least 19 people were injured as Russian missiles and drones hit Kyiv, Zaporizhzhia and Odesa overnight, with strikes recorded at 36 locations and debris falling at five more.
  • Ukraine's Air Force said it destroyed or suppressed 131 aerial targets; a high-rise, a private home and a nursery school were among the damaged civilian sites in Odesa.
  • The barrage landed days after Donald Trump said both sides had agreed to stop hitting energy infrastructure — a truce neither side appears to be observing.
  • Ukraine answered with deep strikes of its own, hitting a refinery in Yaroslavl and damaging warplanes and helicopters at a Rostov airbase, President Zelenskyy said.

Overnight Barrage Hits Three Regions

At least 19 people were injured in Russian missile and drone attacks across Ukraine overnight, officials said on Thursday.

Ukraine's Air Force said it destroyed or suppressed 131 Russian aerial targets during the night, with the main thrust aimed at the Kyiv, Zaporizhzhia and Odesa regions. Strikes were recorded at 36 locations, while debris from intercepted targets fell at five sites.

In Odesa, seven people were injured, including two children, according to Ukraine's State Emergency Service. High-rise apartments in a residential building were damaged, a private residential building was destroyed, and warehouses, a nursery school, cars and garages were hit at other locations, the service said on Telegram.

Kyiv took damage across four districts, including a warehouse and residential buildings in Dniprovsky and another warehouse in Solomyansky. In the surrounding Kyiv region, 33 sites were damaged — 14 in the Brovary district and 10 in Fastiv, according to Tymur Tkachenko, head of the regional administration.

Russia's Defence Ministry said its forces hit metallurgical and electronics plants, military-industrial factories, and energy and transport facilities in the three regions. It also said three bulk carriers and a ferry used to carry supplies for the Ukrainian military were hit in the port of Chornomorsk.

Strikes Land Days After Trump's Energy Truce Claim

The attacks came just days after US President Donald Trump announced that Russia and Ukraine had agreed to suspend strikes on energy facilities, as Trump has blamed the war for pushing up diesel prices around the world.

"Neither Russia nor Ukraine have agreed to this and they are continuing to hit each other's energy targets."

— Rory Challands, Al Jazeera correspondent in Kyiv

Russia, Challands said, is promising to increase its "mass attacks on the Ukrainian energy grid going into the winter months" after last winter's strikes almost collapsed it.

Daytime Barrage Expands

Russia's military, which had previously carried out most attacks at night, has in recent weeks expanded them into daylight hours, A daytime strike on an industrial park near Korosten, west of the capital, killed one person, said Zhytomyr governor Vitali Bunechko.

In Zaporizhzhia, Regional Governor Ivan Fedorov said Russian forces attacked a market, triggering a large blaze; pictures on social media showed the area reduced to charred ruins. A separate attack caused a fire in the southeastern city of Dnipro, injuring two people, while Kyiv mayor Vitali Klitschko said a strike on a non-residential building in the capital injured one.

Ukraine Strikes Back Deep Inside Russia

Kyiv also reported fresh successes in its own long-range campaign. A Ukrainian drone attack hit an oil refinery in the Russian city of Yaroslavl, northeast of Moscow, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said; the resulting fire was extinguished, announced regional governor Mikhail Yevrayev. Zelenskyy also reported damage to Russian warplanes and helicopters in a strike on a military base in the southern city of Rostov.

Moscow said its air defences downed 29 Ukrainian drones heading for the capital, while Russian-appointed Donetsk chief Denis Pushilin said a Ukrainian drone strike on trucks killed three.

Meanwhile, the two sides exchanged the bodies of their war dead: Moscow handed over the remains of 252 people and received 23 in the swap at the Belarusian-Ukrainian border, the Belarusian state news agency BELTA reported.

Indian Students and Workers Still at Risk

The war continues to carry a direct risk for the Indian community in Ukraine. Earlier this month, an Indian citizen was among the dead in a Russian strike on Boryspil, just outside Kyiv, according to Reuters — a reminder that Indians still in the country are not insulated from a war that has again turned daytime.

What's Next

With Russia signalling heavier strikes on the energy grid ahead of winter, Ukraine's air defences face their sternest test since last year. Kyiv says it is critically low on US-made Patriot interceptors capable of stopping ballistic missiles and has urged allies to rush more air-defence systems.

For now, both sides are hitting energy targets, and the fighting shows no sign of pausing.
image_caption: Firefighters work below a Kyiv residential apartment building with shattered windows in the aftermath of a Russian strike. At least 19 people were injured in Russian missile and drone attacks across Ukraine on September 17.
nri_angle: Indian students and workers remain in Ukraine, and an Indian citizen was killed in a Russian strike on Boryspil outside Kyiv earlier this month, according to Reuters.
